segments.t: Welcome to Kukhnya, which means 'The Kitchen', a Russian comedy set in Claude Monet, a smart Moscow restaurant where Chef Barinov rules the kitchen. This episode opens in the middle of the night at Vika's flat, where Max has just crept in very late and Vika is waiting for him. First you'll hear it in Russian, and you don't need to catch every word.
Ты считаешь, что можешь шляться где угодно?
Let's go back through it slowly.
'Woke me up, did you?' One word does the work of four. The 'l' ending tells you it's a man who did it, and 'wake up' is built from the plain word for waking with a prefix on the front.
'Please forgive me.' 'Forgive' is the casual command, and 'me' takes the 'a' form, 'menya'. Max says it the way a child does.
'Where were you, anyway?' 'Anyway' is a long word, 'voobshche', which is said 'vaapshe'. 'Were' ends in 'l' for a man.
'What is this, an interrogation?' 'What kind of' is made with 'chto za', as in many Russian questions. 'Interrogation' is a noun built from 'to ask'.
Ты считаешь, что можешь шляться где угодно?
'You think you can roam wherever you like?' 'Anywhere' is literally 'where it pleases', two words. The slangy word for 'roam' ends in 'sya', so it's 'roam oneself'.
'And come home at three?' Russians say 'in three hours' for 'at three o'clock', and after 'three' 'hour' is shortened. 'Come' is the ongoing kind, for a habit.
'Quarter to.' The Russian is 'without fifteen', since the minutes before the hour are 'without'. Max leaves the hour out, because they both know it's three.
'What kind of relationship do we have?' 'At us' stands for 'we have'. 'Relationship' is always plural in Russian when it means a relationship between two people.
'We have an open relationship.' 'Free' is the Russian for 'open' here, from the same family as 'freedom'. Max says it with a grin.
'It's all fine.' Russian spells 'everything' and 'everyone' the same way when the two dots are left off. Here it clearly means 'everything', so it's 'everything's fine'.
'Since we have an open relationship...' The small word 'raz' means 'since' or 'if it is so'. Vika picks up Max's own words and turns them back on him.

'You're free tonight.' 'Free' is the same as in the 'free relationship', but now a short masculine form. The tiny 'na' in front of 'today' makes it 'for today'. Now let's listen to the whole conversation again from start to finish.
Ты считаешь, что можешь шляться где угодно?

Vika has used Max's own words against him, which is a good way to win an argument. Notice how she turns 'free relationship' into 'you're free tonight', with the same word at the heart of both. See you next time!

lines.fragment: Прости меня, пожалуйста, я так устал.
А, что вообще тут допрос такой, а?
Ты считаешь, что ты можешь шляться, черт знает где, бухать,
а потом приходить спокойно ко мне в три часа?
Все хорошо. Чего ты серьезная такая?
Раз у нас свободные отношения, на сегодня ты свободен.
Раз у нас свободные отношения, на сегодня ты свободен.
